<!-- gate-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the gate catalog and the checker's spec; edit those, not this block -->

Not in the default catalog: `init` does not seed it; a project declares it with `check:`.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Checker | `changelog-valid` |

## How it measures

A product's changelog outputs (`versioning.<product>.changelog.outputs`, VRSNN) are generated by
`anchors changelog --write` (CLGCM), but a file is edited by hand, a template changes, and having
generated it once proves nothing about what it holds later. This gate confronts what each output
holds now.

What does not depend on taste holds for every output:
- each block's marker (CHNGL-B09) reads as a version of the product's scheme;
- the versions come newest first, and none repeats;
- an unreleased block, if any, is on top;
- every tag of the product reachable from HEAD has its block, and every block a tag;
- the block of a release does not change.

The block of the version the sources hold, not released yet, needs no tag: a release pull request
writes it before the tag exists. The change intents waiting for a release (INTNA) are confronted
too.

The rest is the output's `format:`. An output that declares none is held to nothing more.

A release's block that must change, a fix to its text, goes through the commit message's waiver of
the gate, with the reason: the history of a release is not rewritten silently.

```yaml
gates:
  - name: changelog-valid
    check: changelog-valid
    scope: project
    on: [code, docs]
    blocking: true
```

## Declaring it

```yaml
gates:
  - name: changelog-valid
    check: changelog-valid
```
